cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim authority, but A5 pleads for preferential attachment order without treating B responses as approval requests.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 sharpness leads A3 to request first presentation; the question restriction addresses no question, though B4 equality informs A5.

relationship.evidence: B2 prefers a sharper image and B4 offers equal treatment, making B fairness a credible foil for A loyalty test.

heightening.evidence: B4 equal size leads A5 to narrow the demand to opening order and reveal the remembered moving favor.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion poster and A5 moving help establish a concrete choice and personal investment.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 readability cover is rooted in the attachment request; A3 prefabricated authority adds distracting bulk.
